output.brief:
The soft-pedal complaints are most likely caused by contaminated brake fluid, not by drivers or the new pads. Brake fluid at Northfield Motor Services was topped up from a drum opened in March with a missing cap, and it had taken on water. Water-laden fluid boils at low temperature on long descents. Fluid tested at 152°C and 149°C against 255°C for sealed stock. All 11 complaining vans were serviced at Northfield. Vans serviced elsewhere, including the same drivers in other vans on Upper Wend, reported nothing. I am fairly confident, but not certain: the warranty-return evidence is only two vans, and the other Northfield vans are unchecked.

This week: take the 13 Northfield-serviced vans out of service until their fluid is boiling-point tested and renewed from sealed stock. Ask Northfield to recheck the other Larkspur vans it served before 10 September. Do not issue warnings or run descent retraining as a response; that would discourage fault reporting. Do not switch pad suppliers on this evidence. Check that Calder Road and in-house fluid was not the same bulk source.
